claims.explanation: Azaperone is a butyrophenone dopamine D2 antagonist that also has 5-HT2 antagonism and has been shown to inhibit Aβ42 oligomerization; its selective killing pattern is most strongly associated with TP53 mutation and with co-occurring alterations in chromatin/transcription regulators (ARID1A, KMT2D, KMT2C, EP300, CREBBP, SMARCA4) and RTK/RAS-PI3K pathway activation (EGFR, KRAS, PIK3CA, BRAF, PTEN loss), suggesting that cells with defective p53 and epigenetic/transcriptional rewiring are more dependent on dopamine/5-HT receptor signaling or on pathways modulated by azaperone. The pattern is not explained by lineage alone, and the virtual-cell response (steroid receptor, calcium/potassium channel, and protein-synthesis signatures) supports a polypharmacologic mechanism rather than pure DRD2/D

features.basis: TP53 mutation is present in nearly all strongly killed lines and in many weakly affected lines, but its near-universal presence among sensitive lines suggests loss of p53-dependent survival/apoptosis
ARID1A mutation appears in several strongly killed lines (LOXIMVI, SNUC5) and is absent from most weakly affected lines, consistent with SWI/SNF loss creating chromatin-state vulnerability
KMT2D mutation is enriched in strongly killed lines (SNUC5, KYSE270, KE39, HGC27) and rare in weakly affected lines, suggesting epigenetic dependency
KMT2C mutation occurs in multiple strongly killed lines (T3M4, SNUC5, OV7) and is uncommon in the least affected set
EP300 mutation is seen in strongly killed lines (T3M4, SNUC5) and in KU1919 among weakly affected, but its co-occurrence with other chromatin lesions supports a sensitizing role
CREBBP mutation appears in the strongly killed SNUC5 line and is absent from the least affected lines shown
SMARCA4 mutation is present in strongly killed KYSE270 and OV7 lines, consistent with chromatin-remodeler loss increasing drug sensitivity
EGFR mutation is present in several strongly killed lung lines (NCIH1650, HCC95, KYSE270, HCC4006) but also in weakly affected HCC4006, so it is a weaker contextual feature
KRAS mutation appears in strongly killed T3M4, OV7, and SNUC5 lines, suggesting MAPK-pathway activation may cooperate with azaperone effects
PIK3CA mutation is found in strongly killed SNUC5, KYSE510, and HGC27 lines, implicating PI3K-pathway activation in sensitivity
BRAF mutation is present in strongly killed LOXIMVI and SNUC5 lines, though it also appears in weakly affected melanoma lines, making it a weaker feature
PTEN mutation/loss is seen in strongly killed 786O and KALS1 lines, consistent with PI3K-pathway activation contributing to sensitivity
